Sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons: the 2025 [sampling-reliability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) distinguishes agreement with full-catalog evaluation from predictive validity under exposure bias. Uniform negatives often provide weak competition; popularity-based sampling also lacks guaranteed agreement with full ranking. Therefore, retain the pinned 99-negative HR@10 for selection, while using popularity-matched negatives and full-catalog ranking as separate stress tests. Compare model-order agreement across checkpoints/interventions, rather than interpreting sampled HR as a full-catalog estimate.

Embedding collapse is documented in [ICML 2024 research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html), but low effective rank alone does not establish ranking failure or identify a useful intervention. Proposed calibration: measure effective rank, popularity-stratified margins, and final-nonpadding-position next-item performance on training-only temporal holdouts; test whether these diagnostics predict subsequent intervention gains. Define effective rank explicitly, including centering, padding exclusion, and singular-value normalization. [Time to Split (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16289) highlights temporal leakage and target-selection effects; diagnostic holdouts should use earlier prefixes without modifying benchmark splits.

Report all four category HR@10 values and their equal-weight macro average. Use paired user bootstrap resampling within categories for intervention differences, recomputing the macro average each replicate; intervals quantify user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed variation or repeated-search bias. [NIST research](https://www.nist.gov/publications/computing-confidence-intervals-common-ir-measures) supports bootstrap intervals for retrieval measures. With 200 users/category, each hit changes category HR by 0.005. Cache diagnostic cohorts and limit full-catalog checks to selected checkpoints within the GPU budget. No measured diagnostic alignment is available here. Ratings, review text, commercial attributes, and simulator traits remain unavailable; unseen items are unlabeled, not verified negatives.
